oneParagraphVerdict: The chapter has a strong, memorable core: design one peak, mark thresholds, and give endings care without using polish to hide real harm. The red phone, cold-water study, and YES Prep examples make the mechanism clear and transferable, and the layered reads work well for beginners. I would not ship yet because Q3 is structurally ambiguous, but once that quiz item is fixed this is close to professional quality.

items.rationale: The wording directly supports the peak-end memory lesson: a calmer finish can improve recall of the whole visit.
A bright welcome cart is best understood as a vivid, tellable surprise rather than a luxury upgrade or quiet free value.
Both a and b are defensible because the ceremony publicly recognizes effort while naming the next unit also explicitly marks a threshold before logistics take over.
Choice c names elevation, insight, pride, and connection, matching the four ingredients of memorable experiences.
The red-phone lesson is that one visible object can alter the expected script without a full redesign.
The gift becomes memorable when its delivery is staged as a small request-and-reveal event.
The threshold idea supports marking the shared crossing before the group disperses into private next-stage logistics.
The team should not assume equal averaging because recall can overweight the stressful peak and the ending.
The quiet mint disappears because it lacks a tellable format, not because it needs higher cost or better fixtures.
